cohort: The study included 32 pregnancies in 30 women classified as mWHO Class IV with the highest cardiovascular risk, between 2008 and 2022.
finding: Pregnancy in women with mWHO Class IV disease carries substantial risk (65.6% cardiovascular events, 75% preterm birth, 87% NICU admission, 1 maternal death postpartum), but favorable outcomes are achievable in a tertiary center with a specialized Pregnancy Heart Team, though overall morbidity remains high.
mod_finding: All women delivered via Caesarean section, with 93.7% under general anaesthesia.
followup_time: At least 1 year (for MACE rate), with additional long-term follow-up for maternal deaths not specified beyond that.
gest_age: N/A (preterm birth was an outcome, but specific gestational age for the cohort was not provided)
